prior_claim_or_capacity: Exact scalar shift between nested linear specifications
fulltext_evidence: Gelbach defines delta_hat=beta1_base_hat-beta1_full_hat and proves the exact sample OLS identity delta_hat=(X1'X1)^-1 X1'X2 beta2_hat=Gamma_hat beta2_hat; he also defines the population projection target delta=Gamma beta2.
consequence_for_Cplus: C+ must reproduce the finite identity and name the population projection target separately; the IVB-paper sign is reversed by convention.
change_or_limit: Prior algebraic equivalence remains; full text adds direct published evidence and a population target.

prior_claim_or_capacity: Joint decomposition for several possibly correlated controls
fulltext_evidence: Equation 12 decomposes the endpoint into covariate components based on coefficients from the joint full model; mutually exclusive groups sum exactly to the total, and the heterogeneity construction permits many correlated covariates.
consequence_for_Cplus: C+ includes joint-model coefficients and prespecified groups; correlation among controls is not a distinguishing capacity.
change_or_limit: Full text confirms allocation and gives the group-level auxiliary implementation.

prior_claim_or_capacity: Order dependence, leave-one-out and Shapley summaries
fulltext_evidence: The paper demonstrates severe sequence dependence for education and AFQT and replaces sequential increments with conditional full-model components; Appendix D explains the sequence bias. It does not enunciate results about leave-one-out or Shapley in this article.
consequence_for_Cplus: C+ uses Gelbach's single-base conditional allocation for each nested comparison; other allocations require their own decision target.
change_or_limit: Do not attribute the prior LOO/Shapley comparison to Gelbach; it remains the team's synthesis.

fulltext_evidence: The exact matrix identity uses one common Y,X1,X2 system; all NLSY comparisons explicitly use the same 1749 observations. The article does not add a row-hash or audit mechanism.
printed_page_localizers: 515 table 3 note; 521 table 5 note; 525 table 6 note
consequence_for_Cplus: C+ must enforce common rows, transformations and weights for each identity application.
change_or_limit: The software help remains the clearest implementation requirement; full text supplies algebraic and empirical confirmation, not a new audit invariant.

prior_claim_or_capacity: Uncertainty for the paired specification shift
fulltext_evidence: Section IV invokes joint delta-method asymptotics; Appendix B derives four covariance terms for beta2 and Gamma, including cross terms, and permits robust or group-cluster covariance estimators. Note 14 identifies a degenerate zero-variance regime.
consequence_for_Cplus: C+ must use the full joint covariance and distinguish regular, origin-degenerate and cancellation cases. For the B/U and C/U substitution contrasts, their cross-covariance is a deduction from a common stacked system or paired resampling, not a literal Gelbach formula for the trade.
change_or_limit: The paper does not establish block-bootstrap coverage for TSCS, fixed-T validity or uniform inference near the origin.

prior_claim_or_capacity: Meaning of the b1x2 total-change warning
fulltext_evidence: The article derives the mathematical covariance of components but does not discuss the later software display warning for the aggregate __TC row.
consequence_for_Cplus: Keep the prior narrow characterization of the software warning; do not infer a mathematical omission from it.
change_or_limit: No full-text basis to broaden or erase the localized code finding.

fulltext_evidence: The main derivation is OLS. With exact identification of beta1, Gelbach states finite-sample 2SLS equivalence; with overidentification, only asymptotic equivalence under valid instruments; the instrument set is fixed across specifications.
consequence_for_Cplus: If C+ is extended to IV, it must respect exact versus overidentification and fixed instruments. The existing software remains computationally broader on weights and IV.
change_or_limit: Full text supplies theoretical IV scope; details are referred to Gelbach 2009 and were not rederived here.

prior_claim_or_capacity: Interpret a shift as confounding, overcontrol, collider bias or estimand change
fulltext_evidence: Gelbach explicitly distinguishes a population linear projection, which needs no conditional-mean restriction for the algebra, from a causal partial-effect reading under a correctly specified full model. He assumes the full model is substantively appropriate for the decomposition exercise.
consequence_for_Cplus: C+ can attach the same DAG and estimand information as P, while keeping the Gelbach component descriptive when causal conditions fail.
change_or_limit: The article does not provide a general DAG classifier; it also cannot be described as treating causal adequacy as irrelevant.

prior_claim_or_capacity: Use timing and pre-exposure history to classify panel controls
fulltext_evidence: Gelbach notes that timing can sometimes imply a natural causal ordering and discusses AFQT as pre-labor-market while education may be endogenous. His primary domain is cases without a natural order, and he takes the chosen full model as given.
consequence_for_Cplus: C+ receives the same timing/history inputs. A P advantage must be an explicit rule or guarantee for panel history, not awareness that timing matters.
change_or_limit: Full text weakens any claim that Gelbach ignores temporal order, while leaving TSCS history selection undeveloped in this article.

prior_claim_or_capacity: ADL identifies a contemporaneous effect under selection on observables
fulltext_evidence: The Gelbach article does not develop ADL, sequential ignorability or a contemporaneous-effect result in TSCS.
consequence_for_Cplus: C+ must continue to obtain this layer from Blackwell-Glynn and related panel literature.
change_or_limit: No universal absence claim about Gelbach's other work is made.

prior_claim_or_capacity: Unit fixed effects with dynamic treatment and outcomes
fulltext_evidence: The article's regression framework is generic OLS/IV and does not derive a unit-fixed-effects identification result with treatment-outcome feedback.
consequence_for_Cplus: C+ and P both need an external identification derivation for dynamic FE.
change_or_limit: The exact sample identity can survive a common transformation, but it does not determine the fixed-T probability limit.

prior_claim_or_capacity: Projection target, additivity and weights in two-way fixed effects
fulltext_evidence: Gelbach's projection-versus-causal distinction reinforces that an exact coefficient decomposition can remain descriptive; the article does not analyze TWFE comparisons or weights.
consequence_for_Cplus: C+ names the projection target first and imports TWFE causal/weight conditions from Imai-Kim.
change_or_limit: Full text strengthens the target distinction but does not settle the panel estimand.

prior_claim_or_capacity: Lagging a covariate as a response to endogeneity
fulltext_evidence: Gelbach recognizes endogeneity and measurement problems as threats to meaningful decomposition and says valid IV may help if it solves the regression problem; he does not propose lagging as a general cure here.
consequence_for_Cplus: C+ and P must keep persistent dynamics and lag admissibility in the external causal layer.
change_or_limit: No claim is made that Gelbach proves the Bellemare lag result.

prior_claim_or_capacity: Tests involving current X and lagged Y
fulltext_evidence: The two dynamic falsification tests previously mapped to Bellemare are not results developed in this Gelbach article.
consequence_for_Cplus: If used, C+ and P cite and apply the same Bellemare tests with the same one-sided interpretive limits.
change_or_limit: Full-text Gelbach reading neither adds nor removes these external tests.

prior_claim_or_capacity: Move a candidate from lagged state L to contemporary Z
fulltext_evidence: Gelbach proves a decomposition for one nested base-full pair. He does not state the B=(D,W,L), C=(D,W,Z), U=(D,W,L,Z) trade as a single allocation. Applying his identity separately to B/U and C/U and subtracting yields beta_C-beta_B.
printed_page_localizers: 521-523 for each nested identity; B,C,U construction is in the team's derivation
consequence_for_Cplus: C+ can reproduce the trade by two nested applications. The covariance between the two contrast estimates must be derived from their common estimating system or paired resampling.
change_or_limit: Do not call the B,C,U path Gelbach's unique allocation or attribute its cross-contrast covariance formula literally to the article.

fulltext_evidence: Gelbach already provides a user-facing problem, simple auxiliary workflow, grouping, inference and software; he assumes the full specification is chosen and acknowledges special timing-based ordering.
consequence_for_Cplus: A distinct P must add a tested clock/history/decision capacity using the same information as C+, or be characterized as operational/pedagogical.
change_or_limit: General ease of computation and organization are already claimed by Gelbach; TSCS-specific value remains possible but unmeasured.

prior_claim_or_capacity: Novelty boundary for a named estimable decomposition
fulltext_evidence: The full published article is now read. It directly contains the finite and population decompositions, conditional group allocation, joint covariance, nonregular-origin warning, IV extension, Oaxaca-Blinder nesting, Hausman result and cancellation examples.
consequence_for_Cplus: C+ is strengthened; mathematical or inferential novelty of the frozen core remains unsupported. A later claim needs a distinct theorem, guarantee, application result or measured operational gain.
change_or_limit: Status changes from full text unavailable to full text read; substantive overlap is confirmed and expanded rather than reversed.
